summary: For 5-6 year-olds: use a simple model (drawing, diagram, or matching layout) to represent WHY an organism lives where it does, connecting each need (food, water, shelter, suitable conditions) to a feature of its habitat. Children build/use the model, attach a reason to each match, and predict what happens when an organism is placed where its needs aren't met. Includes plants as well as animals. Supports NGSS K-ESS3-1 and leads into UK KS1 'Living things and their habitats'.
misconceptions: Matching animal to place by appearance rather than by needs met.
Thinking any animal can live anywhere.
Believing plants don't have needs or a place they are suited to.
Not connecting a specific need (water, food, shelter) to a specific feature of the place.
Seeing the picture as decoration rather than as a model of a relationship.

activities.title: Connect the needs model: link each need to what the place provides
steps: Look at one organism (e.g. a rabbit) with a few large need-icons beside it: food, water, shelter, warmth.
Draw or drag a link from each need to the part of the habitat that provides it (grass to eat for food, a puddle or stream to drink from for water, a burrow to shelter in and keep warm).
Say aloud the reason for each link: 'the rabbit lives here because there is grass to eat and a burrow to hide in'.
Now try a mismatch: place a fish onto dry sand. Notice its water-need has nothing to connect to, so that link stays unmet and the fish cannot survive there.
Finally, build the model for a NEW animal or plant and say why its home suits it.
activities.insight: An organism lives where it does BECAUSE the place meets its needs; when a need cannot be met, the organism cannot live there.

activities.title: Tap-to-reveal habitat reference: 'this place gives me...'
steps: Tap an organism in a habitat scene (e.g. a rabbit in a meadow) and see what the place provides: grass to eat, a burrow to shelter, space to run.
Tap a fish in a pond to reveal what the pond gives it.
Say back, in your own words, one thing each place provides for that organism.
activities.insight: A habitat supplies specific things that match an organism's specific needs.

activities.title: Match organisms to habitats with a reason, and spot the missing need
steps: Match at least three organisms to the places where their needs are met (e.g. frog to pond, rabbit to meadow, cactus to desert).
For each match, give a need-based reason: 'the frog belongs here because the pond gives it water and insects to eat'.
For a mismatched pair, name which need is missing: 'this place has no water, so the fish's water-need is not met'.
Include at least one plant so the idea of 'needs and a suitable place' is not animals-only.
activities.insight: Matching is correct only when the place meets the organism's needs; a wrong place leaves a specific need unmet.

activities.title: Talking-animal prompt: 'where should I live, and why?'
steps: Listen to an animal ask the child to pick its home.
Choose a place and explain which need each option would meet or miss.
Respond to a follow-up: 'what would happen to me if I lived in the wrong place?'
activities.insight: Choosing a home means reasoning about which needs a place can and cannot meet.

checkQuestion: Show a cactus (lives in the hot, dry desert) and a goldfish (lives in the pond). Ask: 'If I put the cactus into the pond and the fish out into the desert, what would happen to each one? Why does each one live where it does?'
checkAnswer: Both would struggle and die. The fish needs water to breathe and stay wet, so it dies in the dry desert; the cactus is built for very little water and would rot with too much in the pond. Each lives where it does because that place gives it what it needs — the right amount of water and conditions.
